newsitem.title: USA: Merrill's chief economist sees slow Q4 EPS growth.
newsitem.headline: Merrill's chief economist sees slow Q4 EPS growth.

text.p: Merrill Lynch & Co Inc's chief economist Donald Straszheim said he expects profits for top U.S. blue chip companies to fall sharply below Wall Street's expectations in the fourth quarter.

Straszheim expects earnings for the Standard & Poor's 500 companies to grow about two percent in the fourth quarter of 1996 compared with consensus estimates of about 15 percent. For 1997, he expects profits of about three percent.
"We see some some upward pressure on wages and not much pricing power. The result is a margin squeeze and the victim is profits," Straszheim said on a conference call.

"The equity markets will not have the tailwind they had before if interest rates are unchnaged. And if rates decline, a growth rate of two to three percent in earnings is not much of a cushion," he said.

Straszheim expects the U.S. economy to slow, but not stop and for 1996 fourth quarter real Gross Domestic Product (GDP), "we're looking in the 1.5 to 2.0 percent range and for 1997 about the same, in the 2.0 to 2.5 percent range," he said.
"At this point, the economy looks remarkably well- balanced. We simply don't see the end of the current expansion. It will come, but it is not obvious yet."
Straszheim expects an "okay" Christmas shopping season for retailers due to consumer credit restraints and despite some strong indicators, including high consumer confidence and rising real income.
"It's not going to be a blowout season," he said.
He sees the Federal Reserve leaving the fed funds rate unchanged at its upcoming December 17 and February 4-5 meetings of the panel that sets interest rate policy.
"On the long bond for 1997 year overall, we are looking for 6-1/2 minus to seven percent or thereabouts," Straszheim said. -- J. Westhoven, Wall Street Desk, 212 859-1881
